claim: Expressions of voltage-gated sodium channels Nav1.1 and Nav1.2, encoded by SCN1A and SCN2A genes, respectively, have been reported to be mutually exclusive in most brain regions.
source: Expressions of voltage-gated sodium channels Nav1.1 and Nav1.2, encoded by SCN1A and SCN2A genes, respectively, have been reported to be mutually exclusive in most brain regions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a previously reported finding.

claim: In juvenile and adult neocortex, Nav1.1 is predominantly expressed in inhibitory neurons while Nav1.2 is in excitatory neurons.
source: In juvenile and adult neocortex, Nav1.1 is predominantly expressed in inhibitory neurons while Nav1.2 is in excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: A distinct subpopulation of layer V (L5) neocortical excitatory neurons were reported to express Nav1.1.
source: Although a distinct subpopulation of layer V (L5) neocortical excitatory neurons were also reported to express Nav1.1, their nature has been uncharacterized.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a previously reported finding that was uncharacterized.

claim: In hippocampus, Nav1.1 has been proposed to be expressed only in inhibitory neurons.
source: In hippocampus, Nav1.1 has been proposed to be expressed only in inhibitory neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a previous proposal.

claim: The study confirms the mutually exclusive expressions of Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 using newly generated Scn1a-GFP transgenic mouse lines.
source: By using newly generated transgenic mouse lines expressing Scn1a promoter-driven green fluorescent protein (GFP), here we confirm the mutually exclusive expressions of Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 and the absence of Nav1.1 in hippocampal excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Nav1.1 is absent in hippocampal excitatory neurons.
source: By using newly generated transgenic mouse lines expressing Scn1a promoter-driven green fluorescent protein (GFP), here we confirm the mutually exclusive expressions of Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 and the absence of Nav1.1 in hippocampal excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: Nav1.1 is expressed in inhibitory and a subpopulation of excitatory neurons not only in L5 but all layers of neocortex.
source: We also show that Nav1.1 is expressed in inhibitory and a subpopulation of excitatory neurons not only in L5 but all layers of neocortex.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: Most L5 PT neurons express Nav1.1.
source: By using neocortical excitatory projection neuron markers including FEZF2 for L5 pyramidal tract (PT) and TBR1 for layer VI (L6) cortico-thalamic (CT) projection neurons, we further show that most L5 PT neurons and a minor subpopulation of layer II/III (L2/3) cortico-cortical (CC) neurons express Nav1.1 while the majority of L6 CT, L5/6 cortico-striatal (CS), and L2/3 CC neurons express Nav1.2.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data using FEZF2 marker.

claim: A minor subpopulation of layer II/III (L2/3) cortico-cortical (CC) neurons express Nav1.1.
source: By using neocortical excitatory projection neuron markers including FEZF2 for L5 pyramidal tract (PT) and TBR1 for layer VI (L6) cortico-thalamic (CT) projection neurons, we further show that most L5 PT neurons and a minor subpopulation of layer II/III (L2/3) cortico-cortical (CC) neurons express Nav1.1 while the majority of L6 CT, L5/6 cortico-striatal (CS), and L2/3 CC neurons express Nav1.2.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data.

claim: The majority of L6 CT, L5/6 cortico-striatal (CS), and L2/3 CC neurons express Nav1.2.
source: By using neocortical excitatory projection neuron markers including FEZF2 for L5 pyramidal tract (PT) and TBR1 for layer VI (L6) cortico-thalamic (CT) projection neurons, we further show that most L5 PT neurons and a minor subpopulation of layer II/III (L2/3) cortico-cortical (CC) neurons express Nav1.1 while the majority of L6 CT, L5/6 cortico-striatal (CS), and L2/3 CC neurons express Nav1.2.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data using TBR1 marker.

claim: Voltage-gated sodium channels play crucial roles in the generation and propagation of action potentials, contributing to excitability and information processing.
source: Voltage-gated sodium channels (VGSCs) play crucial roles in the generation and propagation of action potentials, contributing to excitability and information processing (Catterall, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Catterall, 2012.

claim: VGSCs consist of one main pore-forming alpha- and one or two subsidiary beta-subunits that regulate kinetics or subcellular trafficking of the alpha subunits.
source: They consist of one main pore-forming alpha- and one or two subsidiary beta-subunits that regulate kinetics or subcellular trafficking of the alpha subunits.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about VGSC structure.

claim: Human has nine alpha (Nav1.1–Nav1.9) and four beta (beta-1–beta-4) subunits.
source: Human has nine alpha (Nav1.1–Nav1.9) and four beta (beta-1–beta-4) subunits.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Nav1.1, Nav1.2, Nav1.3, and Nav1.6, encoded by SCN1A, SCN2A, SCN3A, and SCN8A, respectively, are expressed in central nervous system.
source: Among alphas, Nav1.1, Nav1.2, Nav1.3, and Nav1.6, encoded by SCN1A, SCN2A, SCN3A, and SCN8A, respectively, are expressed in central nervous system.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: SCN3A is mainly expressed embryonically.
source: SCN3A is mainly expressed embryonically (Brysch et al., 1991), and SCN1A, SCN2A, and SCN8A are major alphas after birth.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Brysch et al., 1991.

claim: SCN1A, SCN2A, and SCN8A are major alphas after birth.
source: SCN3A is mainly expressed embryonically (Brysch et al., 1991), and SCN1A, SCN2A, and SCN8A are major alphas after birth.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: SCN1A and SCN2A show mutations in a wide spectrum of neurological diseases such as epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and intellectual disability.
source: Although these three genes show mutations in a wide spectrum of neurological diseases such as epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and intellectual disability, two of those, SCN1A and SCN2A, are major ones (reviewed in Yamakawa, 2016; Meisler et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Yamakawa, 2016 and Meisler et al., 2021.

claim: Expressions of Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 seem to be mutually exclusive in many brain regions.
source: We previously reported that expressions of Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 seem to be mutually exclusive in many brain regions (Yamagata et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Yamagata et al., 2017.

claim: In adult neocortex and hippocampus, Nav1.1 is dominantly expressed in medial ganglionic eminence-derived parvalbumin-positive (PV-IN) and somatostatin-positive (SST-IN) inhibitory neurons.
source: In adult neocortex and hippocampus, Nav1.1 is dominantly expressed in medial ganglionic eminence-derived parvalbumin-positive (PV-IN) and somatostatin-positive (SST-IN) inhibitory neurons (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Lorincz and Nusser, 2008; Ogiwara et al., 2013; Li et al., 2014; Tai et al., 2014; Tian et al., 2014; Yamagata et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations.

claim: Some amount of Nav1.1 is expressed in a distinct subset of layer V (L5) excitatory neurons in the neocortex.
source: In the neocortex, some amount of Nav1.1 is also expressed in a distinct subset of layer V (L5) excitatory neurons (Ogiwara et al., 2013), but their natures were unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Ogiwara et al., 2013.

claim: Nav1.1 seems to be expressed in inhibitory but not in excitatory neurons in the hippocampus.
source: In the hippocampus, Nav1.1 seems to be expressed in inhibitory but not in excitatory neurons (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Ogiwara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to Ogiwara et al., 2007 and Ogiwara et al., 2013.

claim: A major amount of Nav1.2 (~95%) is expressed in excitatory neurons including the most of neocortical and all of hippocampal ones.
source: In contrast, a major amount of Nav1.2 (~95%) is expressed in excitatory neurons including the most of neocortical and all of hippocampal ones, and a minor amount is expressed in caudal ganglionic eminence-derived inhibitory neurons such as vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP)-positive ones (Lorincz and Nusser, 2010; Yamagata et al., 2017; Ogiwara et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: A minor amount of Nav1.2 is expressed in caudal ganglionic eminence-derived inhibitory neurons such as vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP)-positive ones.
source: In contrast, a major amount of Nav1.2 (~95%) is expressed in excitatory neurons including the most of neocortical and all of hippocampal ones, and a minor amount is expressed in caudal ganglionic eminence-derived inhibitory neurons such as vasoactive intestinal polypeptide (VIP)-positive ones (Lorincz and Nusser, 2010; Yamagata et al., 2017; Ogiwara et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: A subpopulation (more than half) of VIP-positive inhibitory neurons is Nav1.1-positive.
source: However, a recent study reported that a subpopulation (more than half) of VIP-positive inhibitory neurons is Nav1.1-positive (Goff and Goldberg, 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to Goff and Goldberg, 2019.

claim: Scn1a-GFP founder mice were generated from C57BL/6J zygotes microinjected with a modified Scn1a-GFP BAC construct.
source: Scn1a-GFP founder mice were generated from C57BL/6J zygotes microinjected with a modified Scn1a-GFP BAC construct harboring all, upstream and downstream, Scn1a promoters (Nakayama et al., 2010; Figure 1A) (see Materials and methods for details).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Western blot analysis showed robust GFP expression in Scn1a-GFP mouse lines #184 and #233.
source: Western blot analysis (Figure 1B) and immunohistochemistry (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) showed robust GFP expression and mostly normal expression levels of Nav1.1 in Scn1a-GFP mouse lines #184 and #233.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Scn1a-GFP mouse lines #184 and #233 showed mostly normal expression levels of Nav1.1.
source: Western blot analysis (Figure 1B) and immunohistochemistry (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) showed robust GFP expression and mostly normal expression levels of Nav1.1 in Scn1a-GFP mouse lines #184 and #233.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Both Scn1a-GFP lines #184 and #233 showed a similar distribution of chromogenic GFP immunosignals across the entire brain.
source: Both lines showed a similar distribution of chromogenic GFP immunosignals across the entire brain (Figure 2A–H), and a similar distribution was also obtained in fluorescence detection of GFP (Figure 2I–L and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: In neocortex, GFP-positive cells were distributed throughout all cortical layers in Scn1a-GFP mice.
source: In neocortex (Figure 2B, F, J and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B, F), GFP-positive cells were distributed throughout all cortical layers.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Cells with intense GFP signals in hippocampus are assumed to be PV-IN and SST-IN.
source: In hippocampus (Figure 2C, G, K and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, G), cells with intense GFP signals, which are assumed to be PV-IN and SST-IN (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Tai et al., 2014) (see also Figure 8), were scattered in stratum oriens, pyramidale, radiatum, lucidum, and lacunosum-moleculare of the CA (cornu ammonis) fields, hilus and molecular layer of dentate gyrus.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and reference to Figure 8.

claim: Somata of dentate granule cells were apparently GFP-negative.
source: Of note, somata of dentate granule cells were apparently GFP-negative.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: CA1–3 pyramidal cells were twined around with fibrous GFP immunosignals.
source: CA1–3 pyramidal cells were twined around with fibrous GFP immunosignals.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: The fibrous Nav1.1 signals clinging to somata of hippocampal CA1–3 pyramidal cells are axon terminals of PV-INs.
source: We previously reported that the fibrous Nav1.1 signals clinging to somata of hippocampal CA1–3 pyramidal cells were disappeared by conditional elimination of Nav1.1 in PV-INs but not in excitatory neurons, and therefore concluded that these Nav1.1-immunopositive fibers are axon terminals of PV-INs (Ogiwara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to Ogiwara et al., 2013.

claim: CA pyramidal cells themselves are assumed to be GFP-negative.
source: As such, GFP signals are fibrous but do not form cell shapes in the CA pyramidal cell layer (Figure 2C, G, K and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, G), and therefore these CA pyramidal cells themselves are assumed to be GFP-negative.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an inference from the observation.

claim: Hippocampal excitatory neurons are negative for Nav1.1.
source: These observations further confirmed our previous proposal that hippocampal excitatory neurons are negative for Nav1.1 (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Ogiwara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: In cerebellum, GFP signals appeared in Purkinje, basket, and deep cerebellar nuclei cells.
source: In cerebellum (Figure 2D, H, L and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D, H), GFP signals appeared in Purkinje, basket, and deep cerebellar nuclei cells, again consistent to the previous reports (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Ogiwara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Quantification of Nav1.1 signals in western blot analyses showed no difference between Scn1a-GFP mice and their wild-type littermates.
source: Quantification of Nav1.1 signals in western blot analyses of brain lysates from the Scn1a-GFP mice and their wild-type littermates (N = 5 animals per each genotype) showed no difference between genotypes, while that of GFP somehow deviated among individual Scn1a-GFP mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: GFP signals continue to be intense in caudal region such as thalamus, midbrain, and brainstem at P15, 4W and 8W.
source: Fluorescence imaging of the Scn1a-GFP sagittal brain sections at postnatal day 15 (P15), 4-week-old (4W) and 8W showed that GFP signals continue to be intense in caudal region such as thalamus, midbrain, and brainstem (Figure 3), which is well consistent with our previous report of Nav1.1 protein and Scn1a mRNA distributions in wild-type mouse brain (Ogiwara et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Figure 3.

claim: GFP-positive cells occupy 30% (L2/3), 32% (L5), and 22% (L6) of NeuN- and GFP-positive cells at P15.
source: The NeuN staining showed that GFP-positive cells occupy 30% (L2/3), 32% (L5), and 22% (L6) of NeuN- and GFP-positive cells at P15 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B and Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Sparsely distributed cells with intense GFP signals, which are assumed to be PV-INs, were often NeuN-negative.
source: However, we noticed that sparsely distributed cells with intense GFP signals, which are assumed to be PV-INs (see Figure 8), were often NeuN-negative (Figure 3—figure supplement 2 – arrowheads), reminiscent of a previous report that NeuN expression is absent in cerebellar inhibitory neurons such as Golgi, basket, and satellite cells in cerebellum (Weyer and Schilling, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: 17% (L2/3), 21% (L5), and 8% (L6) of neurons (cells with ankyrinG-positive AISs) were GFP-positive.
source: Cell counting revealed that 17% (L2/3), 21% (L5), and 8% (L6) of neurons (cells with ankyrinG-positive AISs) were GFP-positive (Figure 4D, left panel and Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: All cells with Nav1.1-positive AISs or somata were GFP-positive.
source: Of note, all cells with Nav1.1-positive AISs or somata were GFP-positive, but AISs or somata for only half of GFP-positive cells were Nav1.1-positive (Figure 4D and Supplementary file 1c, d), possibly due to undetectably low levels of Nav1.1 immunosignals in a subpopulation of GFP-positive cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: AISs or somata for only half of GFP-positive cells were Nav1.1-positive, possibly due to undetectably low levels of Nav1.1 immunosignals in a subpopulation of GFP-positive cells.
source: Of note, all cells with Nav1.1-positive AISs or somata were GFP-positive, but AISs or somata for only half of GFP-positive cells were Nav1.1-positive (Figure 4D and Supplementary file 1c, d), possibly due to undetectably low levels of Nav1.1 immunosignals in a subpopulation of GFP-positive cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Averaged ratios of GFP-positive cells among neurons are 23% (L2/3), 26% (L5), and 13% (L6).
source: Averaged ratios of GFP-positive cells among neurons of these experiments are 23% (L2/3), 26% (L5), and 13% (L6) (Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1f), which are actually significantly lower than those obtained in the NeuN staining (Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: All GFP-positive cells were Nav1.1-positive in the hippocampus.
source: In contrast to the neocortex where only half of GFP-positive cells were Nav1.1-positive, in the hippocampus all GFP-positive cells were Nav1.1-positive and all Nav1.1-positive cells were GFP-positive (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: All Nav1.1-positive cells were GFP-positive in the hippocampus.
source: In contrast to the neocortex where only half of GFP-positive cells were Nav1.1-positive, in the hippocampus all GFP-positive cells were Nav1.1-positive and all Nav1.1-positive cells were GFP-positive (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5.

claim: Most of excitatory neurons such as CA1–3 pyramidal cells and dentate granule cells were GFP-negative.
source: Actually, most of excitatory neurons such as CA1–3 pyramidal cells and dentate granule cells were GFP-negative.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: 98% of cells with GFP-positive somata were Nav1.1-positive at their AISs in hippocampal CA1 region.
source: Cell counting in the hippocampal CA1 region showed that 98% of cells with GFP-positive somata were Nav1.1-positive at their AISs and 100% of cells with Nav1.1-positive AISs were GFP-positive (Figure 5F and Supplementary file 1g, h).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: 100% of cells with Nav1.1-positive AISs were GFP-positive in hippocampal CA1 region.
source: Cell counting in the hippocampal CA1 region showed that 98% of cells with GFP-positive somata were Nav1.1-positive at their AISs and 100% of cells with Nav1.1-positive AISs were GFP-positive (Figure 5F and Supplementary file 1g, h).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Double in situ hybridization of Scn1a and GFP mRNAs showed that these signals well overlap in both neocortex and hippocampus of Scn1a-GFP mice.
source: Double in situ hybridization of Scn1a and GFP mRNAs showed that these signals well overlap in both neocortex and hippocampus of Scn1a-GFP mice (Figure 6), further supporting that the GFP signals well represent endogenous Scn1a/Nav1.1 expression.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 6.

claim: In neocortex, Scn1a and GFP mRNAs seem to be expressed in a number of neurons including some of excitatory pyramidal cells.
source: Again, in neocortex Scn1a and GFP mRNAs seem to be expressed in a number of neurons including some of excitatory pyramidal cells, while in hippocampus they are absent in excitatory neurons such as CA1–3 pyramidal cells and dentate granule cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: In hippocampus, Scn1a and GFP mRNAs are absent in excitatory neurons such as CA1–3 pyramidal cells and dentate granule cells.
source: Again, in neocortex Scn1a and GFP mRNAs seem to be expressed in a number of neurons including some of excitatory pyramidal cells, while in hippocampus they are absent in excitatory neurons such as CA1–3 pyramidal cells and dentate granule cells.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: 23% (L2/3), 28% (L5), and 27% (L6) of GFP-positive cells were Tomato-positive inhibitory neurons in the neocortex at 4W.
source: In the neocortex at 4W, 23% (L2/3), 28% (L5), and 27% (L6) of GFP-positive cells were Tomato-positive inhibitory neurons and 73% (L2/3), 77% (L5), and 83% (L6) of Tomato-positive cells were GFP-positive (Figure 7C and Supplementary file 1i, j).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: 73% (L2/3), 77% (L5), and 83% (L6) of Tomato-positive cells were GFP-positive in the neocortex at 4W.
source: In the neocortex at 4W, 23% (L2/3), 28% (L5), and 27% (L6) of GFP-positive cells were Tomato-positive inhibitory neurons and 73% (L2/3), 77% (L5), and 83% (L6) of Tomato-positive cells were GFP-positive (Figure 7C and Supplementary file 1i, j).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: A significant subpopulation of neocortical excitatory neurons also express Nav1.1.
source: These results suggest that a significant subpopulation of neocortical excitatory neurons also express Nav1.1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: In the hippocampus, most of GFP-positive cells were Tomato-positive, 98% (CA1) and 94% (DG).
source: Unlike in neocortex, in the hippocampus most of GFP-positive cells were Tomato-positive, 98% (CA1) and 94% (DG), and majorities of Tomato-positive GABAergic neurons are GFP-positive, 93% (CA1) and 77% (DG).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: Majorities of Tomato-positive GABAergic neurons are GFP-positive in the hippocampus, 93% (CA1) and 77% (DG).
source: Unlike in neocortex, in the hippocampus most of GFP-positive cells were Tomato-positive, 98% (CA1) and 94% (DG), and majorities of Tomato-positive GABAergic neurons are GFP-positive, 93% (CA1) and 77% (DG).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: In hippocampus, Nav1.1 is expressed in inhibitory neurons but not in excitatory neurons.
source: These results further confirmed that in hippocampus Nav1.1 is expressed in inhibitory neurons but not in excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: PV-INs and SST-INs were both GFP-positive.
source: PV-INs and SST-INs were both GFP-positive, and especially GFP signals in PV-INs were intense (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8A.

claim: GFP signals in PV-INs were intense.
source: PV-INs and SST-INs were both GFP-positive, and especially GFP signals in PV-INs were intense (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8A.

claim: 21% (L2/3), 37% (L5), 37% (L6), 58% (CA1), 42% (CA2/3), and 41% (DG) of GFP-positive cells were PV- or SST-positive depending on regions in neocortex and hippocampus.
source: Cell counting revealed that 21% (L2/3), 37% (L5), 37% (L6), 58% (CA1), 42% (CA2/3), and 41% (DG) of GFP-positive cells were PV- or SST-positive depending on regions in neocortex and hippocampus (Figure 8B and Supplementary file 1k–m).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: All PV-INs were GFP-positive.
source: All PV-INs were GFP-positive (Figure 8B, middle), and most of SST-INs were GFP-positive (Figure 8B, right).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: Most of SST-INs were GFP-positive.
source: All PV-INs were GFP-positive (Figure 8B, middle), and most of SST-INs were GFP-positive (Figure 8B, right).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 8B.

claim: GFP-positive GABAergic neurons in neocortex are mostly PV- or SST-positive.
source: Comparison of these results with those of Slc32a1-Cre mouse (Figure 7) suggests that GFP-positive GABAergic neurons in neocortex are mostly PV- or SST-positive, while in hippocampus a half of those are PV/SST-negative GABAergic neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: In hippocampus, a half of GFP-positive GABAergic neurons are PV/SST-negative GABAergic neurons.
source: Comparison of these results with those of Slc32a1-Cre mouse (Figure 7) suggests that GFP-positive GABAergic neurons in neocortex are mostly PV- or SST-positive, while in hippocampus a half of those are PV/SST-negative GABAergic neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: GFP signal intensities in PV-positive cells were significantly higher than those in PV-negative cells.
source: Quantitative analysis of GFP signal intensity and area size of cells revealed that GFP signal intensities in PV-positive cells were significantly higher than those in PV-negative cells and GFP signal intensities in SST-positive cells were lower than those in PV-positive cells but similar to PV/SST-double negative cells (Figure 9 and Supplementary file 1n–p).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9.

claim: GFP signal intensities in SST-positive cells were lower than those in PV-positive cells but similar to PV/SST-double negative cells.
source: Quantitative analysis of GFP signal intensity and area size of cells revealed that GFP signal intensities in PV-positive cells were significantly higher than those in PV-negative cells and GFP signal intensities in SST-positive cells were lower than those in PV-positive cells but similar to PV/SST-double negative cells (Figure 9 and Supplementary file 1n–p).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 9.

claim: Nav1.1 expression level in PV-INs is significantly higher than those in excitatory neurons and PV-negative GABAergic neurons including SST-INs.
source: These results indicate that Nav1.1 expression level in PV-INs is significantly higher than those in excitatory neurons and PV-negative GABAergic neurons including SST-INs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Expressions of Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 are mutually exclusive in brain regions including neocortex.
source: The staining again showed that Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 expressions are mutually exclusive in brain regions including neocortex (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 10A.

claim: 5% (L2/3), 6% (L5), and 3% (L6) of AISs at P15 were Nav1.1-positive in the neocortex.
source: The counting revealed that 5% (L2/3), 6% (L5), and 3% (L6) of AISs at P15 were Nav1.1-positive and 78% (L2/3), 69% (L5), and 69% (L6) of AISs at P15 were Nav1.2-positive in the neocortex (Figure 10B and Supplementary file 1q).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 10B.

claim: 78% (L2/3), 69% (L5), and 69% (L6) of AISs at P15 were Nav1.2-positive in the neocortex.
source: The counting revealed that 5% (L2/3), 6% (L5), and 3% (L6) of AISs at P15 were Nav1.1-positive and 78% (L2/3), 69% (L5), and 69% (L6) of AISs at P15 were Nav1.2-positive in the neocortex (Figure 10B and Supplementary file 1q).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Less than 0.5% of AISs are Nav1.1/Nav1.2-double positive.
source: Of note, less than 0.5% of AISs are Nav1.1/Nav1.2-double positive confirming that Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 do not co-express.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 do not co-express.
source: Of note, less than 0.5% of AISs are Nav1.1/Nav1.2-double positive confirming that Nav1.1 and Nav1.2 do not co-express.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: 88% (L2/3), 90% (L5), and 95% (L6) of cells with Nav1.2-positive AISs at P15 were GFP-negative.

claim: 69% (L2/3), 83% (L5), and 86% (L6) of AISs of GFP-positive cells at P15 were Nav1.2-negative.

claim: FEZF2 is expressed in L5 PT neurons, forms their axonal projections, and defines their targets.
source: A transcription factor FEZF2 is expressed in L5 PT neurons, forms their axonal projections, and defines their targets (Inoue et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2005; Chen et al., 2008; Lodato et al., 2014).

claim: Most of PT neurons are FEZF2-positive.
source: Most of PT neurons are FEZF2-positive (Molyneaux et al., 2005; Matho et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: 83% and 96% of FEZF2-positive neurons were GFP-positive at P15 and 4W, respectively, in L5.
source: In L5 where a major population of FEZF2-positive cells locate (Figure 12A), a majority of FEZF2-positive neurons were GFP-positive (83% and 96% of FEZF2-positive neurons were GFP-positive at P15 and 4W, respectively) (Figure 12B, middle panels and Supplementary file 1v).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 12B.

claim: FEZF2/GFP-double positive cells in L5 showed significantly lower GFP immunosignal intensities and larger signal areas (soma sizes) compared to those of FEZF2-negative/GFP-positive cells.
source: Quantitative analyses revealed that FEZF2/GFP-double positive cells in L5 showed significantly lower GFP immunosignal intensities and larger signal areas (soma sizes) compared to those of FEZF2-negative/GFP-positive cells (Figure 13 and Supplementary file 1x), indicating that L5 PT neurons showed lower Nav1.1 expression compared to other neurons such as PV-INs (see also Figure 9).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 13.

claim: L5 PT neurons showed lower Nav1.1 expression compared to other neurons such as PV-INs.
source: Quantitative analyses revealed that FEZF2/GFP-double positive cells in L5 showed significantly lower GFP immunosignal intensities and larger signal areas (soma sizes) compared to those of FEZF2-negative/GFP-positive cells (Figure 13 and Supplementary file 1x), indicating that L5 PT neurons showed lower Nav1.1 expression compared to other neurons such as PV-INs (see also Figure 9).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: 11% of FEZF2-positive cells have Nav1.1-positive AIS in L5 of Scn1a-GFP mouse neocortex.
source: We further performed triple immunostaining of FEZF2, Nav1.1, and ankyrinG on Scn1a-GFP mice at P15, and found that 11% of FEZF2-positive cells have Nav1.1-positive AIS in L5 of Scn1a-GFP mouse neocortex (Figure 12—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1y, z, aa).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 12—figure supplement 1.

claim: The low ratios of FEZF2/Nav1.1-double positive cells are most possibly due to immunohistochemically undetectable low levels of Nav1.1 expression in these excitatory neurons.
source: The low ratios of FEZF2/Nav1.1-double positive cells are most possibly due to immunohistochemically undetectable low levels of Nav1.1 expression in these excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: 20% of neurons (cells with ankyrinG-positive AISs) in L5 are FEZF2-positive.
source: The staining showed that 20% of neurons (cells with ankyrinG-positive AISs) in L5 are FEZF2-positive and a half of L5 FEZF2-positive cells have Nav1.2-positive AISs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: A half of L5 FEZF2-positive cells have Nav1.2-positive AISs.
source: The staining showed that 20% of neurons (cells with ankyrinG-positive AISs) in L5 are FEZF2-positive and a half of L5 FEZF2-positive cells have Nav1.2-positive AISs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation.

claim: A subpopulation of FEZF2-positive PT neurons may express both Nav1.1 and Nav1.2.
source: Together with the observation that most of FEZF2-positive cells are GFP-positive (Figure 12), these results indicate that a subpopulation of FEZF2-positive PT neurons may express both Nav1.1 and Nav1.2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The majority of L5 PT neurons express Nav1.1.
source: Although further studies such retrograde tracking analyses are required to confirm and figure out the detailed circuits, all these results propose that the majority of L5 PT neurons express Nav1.1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a proposal based on the data.

claim: TBR1 is a negative regulator of FEZF2 and therefore not expressed in the PT neurons.
source: TBR1 (T-box brain 1 transcription factor) is a negative regulator of FEZF2 and therefore not expressed in the PT neurons, all of which are known to be FEZF2-positive (Chen et al., 2008; Han et al., 2011; McKenna et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: TBR1 is predominantly expressed in L6 CT neurons and subpopulations of L2/3 and L5 non-PT excitatory neurons.
source: TBR1 is predominantly expressed in L6 CT neurons and subpopulations of L2/3 and L5 non-PT excitatory neurons instead (Han et al., 2011; McKenna et al., 2011; Matho et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: The ratios of GFP-positive cells among TBR1-positive cells are 11% at P15 and 5% at 4W in L5.
source: In L5, contrary to the high ratios of GFP-positive cells among FEZF2-positive cells (83% at P15 and 96% at 4W) (Figure 12B), the ratios of GFP-positive cells among TBR1-positive cells are quite low (11% at P15 and 5% at 4W) (Figure 14B, middle panels and Supplementary file 1ah).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 14B.

claim: The ratios of GFP-positive cells among TBR1-positive cells are 15% at P15 and 26% at 4W in L6.
source: In L6 where a major population of TBR1-positive neurons locate, the ratios of GFP-positive cells among TBR1-positive cells are still low (15% at P15 and 26% at 4W) (Figure 14B, middle panels and Supplementary file 1ah).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 14B.

claim: The ratios of Nav1.1-positive cells among TBR1-positive cells are 0% in all layers.
source: Notably, the ratios of Nav1.1-positive cells among TBR1-positive cells are 0% in all layers (Figure 14—figure supplement 1B, right panel and Supplementary file 1am).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 14—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The major population of TBR1-positive cells do not express Nav1.1.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The ratios of Nav1.2-positive cells among TBR1-positive cells are 69% (L2/3), 69%(L5), and 69% (L6) at P15.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 14—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Most TBR1-positive neurons including L6 CT neurons do not express Nav1.1 but expresses Nav1.2.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that most TBR1-positive neurons including L6 CT neurons do not express Nav1.1 but expresses Nav1.2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: A minor subpopulation of L2/3 CC and L5 PT neurons express Nav1.1 while the majority of L2/3 CC, L5/6 CS, and L6 CT neurons express Nav1.2.
source: As a whole, above results showed that a minor subpopulation of L2/3 CC and L5 PT neurons express Nav1.1 while the majority of L2/3 CC, L5/6 CS, and L6 CT neurons express Nav1.2.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the findings.

claim: All PV-INs and most of SST-INs were GFP-positive in the neocortex and hippocampus of the Scn1a-GFP mouse.
source: All PV-INs and most of SST-INs were GFP-positive in the neocortex and hippocampus of the Scn1a-GFP mouse, being consistent with the previous reports of Nav1.1 expression in those inhibitory neurons (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Lorincz and Nusser, 2008; Ogiwara et al., 2013; Li et al., 2014; Tai et al., 2014; Tian et al., 2014; Yamagata et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: All Nav1.1-positive cells were GFP-positive.

evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a finding.

claim: In the hippocampus, Nav1.1 expression is restricted to inhibitory neurons.
source: This is largely because in the hippocampus Nav1.1 expression is restricted to inhibitory neurons, but in the neocortex Nav1.1 is expressed not only in inhibitory but also in a subpopulation of excitatory neurons in which Nav1.1 expression is low and not easily detected immunohistochemically by anti-Nav1.1 antibodies.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation of the findings.

evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an explanation of the findings.

source: In neocortex, one-third of GFP-positive cells were GABAergic cells such as PV-INs and SST-INs, and the remaining two-third were excitatory neurons.

claim: Dravet syndrome is a sporadic intractable epileptic encephalopathy characterized by early onset (6 months to 1 year after birth) epileptic seizures, intellectual disability, autistic features, ataxia, and increased risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP).
source: Dravet syndrome is a sporadic intractable epileptic encephalopathy characterized by early onset (6 months to 1 year after birth) epileptic seizures, intellectual disability, autistic features, ataxia, and increased risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as established knowledge.

claim: De novo loss-of-function mutations of SCN1A are found in more than 80% of Dravet syndrome patients.
source: De novo loss-of-function mutations of SCN1A are found in more than 80% of the patients (Claes et al., 2001; Sugawara et al., 2002; Fujiwara et al., 2003; Dravet et al., 2005; Depienne et al., 2009; Meng et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: In mice, loss-of-function Scn1a mutations caused clinical features reminiscent of Dravet syndrome, including early-onset epileptic seizures, hyperactivity, learning and memory deficits, reduced sociability and ataxic gaits and premature sudden death.
source: In mice, loss-of-function Scn1a mutations caused clinical features reminiscent of Dravet syndrome, including early-onset epileptic seizures, hyperactivity, learning and memory deficits, reduced sociability and ataxic gaits and premature sudden death (Yu et al., 2006; Ogiwara et al., 2007; Oakley et al., 2009; Cao et al., 2012; Han et al., 2012; Kalume et al., 2013; Ito et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Nav1.1 is densely localized at AISs of inhibitory cells such PV-IN.
source: As also shown in the present study, Nav1.1 is densely localized at AISs of inhibitory cells such PV-IN (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Ogiwara et al., 2013; Li et al., 2014; Tai et al., 2014) and selective elimination of Nav1.1 in PV-IN in mice leads to epileptic seizures, sudden death, and deficits in social behavior and spatial memory (Ogiwara et al., 2013; Tatsukawa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Selective elimination of Nav1.1 in PV-IN in mice leads to epileptic seizures, sudden death, and deficits in social behavior and spatial memory.
source: As also shown in the present study, Nav1.1 is densely localized at AISs of inhibitory cells such PV-IN (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Ogiwara et al., 2013; Li et al., 2014; Tai et al., 2014) and selective elimination of Nav1.1 in PV-IN in mice leads to epileptic seizures, sudden death, and deficits in social behavior and spatial memory (Ogiwara et al., 2013; Tatsukawa et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Nav1.1 haplo-deficiency in PV-IN plays a pivotal role in the pathophysiology of many clinical aspects of Dravet syndrome.
source: It is thus plausible that Nav1.1 haplo-deficiency in PV-IN plays a pivotal role in the pathophysiology of many clinical aspects of Dravet syndrome.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data.

claim: Mice with selective Nav1.1 reduction in global inhibitory neurons were at a greater risk of lethal seizure than heterozygote null mice (Nav1.1 KO/+).
source: Notably, mice with selective Nav1.1 reduction in global inhibitory neurons were at a greater risk of lethal seizure than heterozygote null mice (Nav1.1 KO/+), and the mortality risk of mice with Nav1.1 haplo-deficiency in inhibitory neurons was significantly decreased or improved with additional Nav1.1 reduction in dorsal telencephalic excitatory neurons (Ogiwara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Ogiwara et al., 2013.

claim: The mortality risk of mice with Nav1.1 haplo-deficiency in inhibitory neurons was significantly decreased or improved with additional Nav1.1 reduction in dorsal telencephalic excitatory neurons.
source: Notably, mice with selective Nav1.1 reduction in global inhibitory neurons were at a greater risk of lethal seizure than heterozygote null mice (Nav1.1 KO/+), and the mortality risk of mice with Nav1.1 haplo-deficiency in inhibitory neurons was significantly decreased or improved with additional Nav1.1 reduction in dorsal telencephalic excitatory neurons (Ogiwara et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Ogiwara et al., 2013.

claim: Nav1.1 deficiency in excitatory neurons has beneficial effects for epileptic seizures and sudden death.
source: These observations indicate beneficial effects of Nav1.1 deficiency in excitatory neurons for epileptic seizures and sudden death.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: The ameliorating effect was most possibly caused by Nav1.1 haploinsufficiency in neocortical excitatory neurons.
source: Because of the absence of Nav1.1 in hippocampal excitatory neurons (Ogiwara et al., 2007; Ogiwara et al., 2013; Yamagata et al., 2017) and the present study, the ameliorating effect was most possibly caused by Nav1.1 haploinsufficiency in neocortical excitatory neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the data.

claim: Parasympathetic hyperactivity is observed in Nav1.1 haplo-deficient mice and it causes ictal bradycardia and finally result in seizure-associated sudden death.
source: Kalume et al., 2013 reported that parasympathetic hyperactivity is observed in Nav1.1 haplo-deficient mice and it causes ictal bradycardia and finally result in seizure-associated sudden death.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Kalume et al., 2013.

claim: Impaired CS excitatory neurotransmission causes epilepsies in Scn2a haplo-deficient mouse.
source: We previously proposed that impaired CS excitatory neurotransmission causes epilepsies in Scn2a haplo-deficient mouse (Miyamoto et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to Miyamoto et al., 2019.

claim: SCN2A has been well established as one of top genes which show de novo loss-of-function mutations in patients with ASD.
source: Because SCN2A has been well established as one of top genes which show de novo loss-of-function mutations in patients with ASD (Hoischen et al., 2014; Johnson et al., 2016) and because impaired striatal function was suggested in multiple ASD animal models (Fuccillo, 2016), our finding of Nav1.2 expression in CS neurons may also contribute to the understanding of neural circuit for ASD caused by SCN2A mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: Impaired striatal function was suggested in multiple ASD animal models.
source: Because SCN2A has been well established as one of top genes which show de novo loss-of-function mutations in patients with ASD (Hoischen et al., 2014; Johnson et al., 2016) and because impaired striatal function was suggested in multiple ASD animal models (Fuccillo, 2016), our finding of Nav1.2 expression in CS neurons may also contribute to the understanding of neural circuit for ASD caused by SCN2A mutations.
